subject: Urgent: Cadenza production degradation after v4-compact rollout
messages:
From: Sam Tan <sam.tan@cadenza.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production alert — marked latency & errors after last-night rollout

Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

We're seeing a severe degradation in our production inference traffic since the new v4-compact quantization profile was rolled out across our dedicated pool at ~02:30 UTC last night. Key signals:
- p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to ~980ms during peak windows.
- Error rate rose to ~3.4% (was ~0.1%).
- Serving throughput dropped ~40% despite roughly the same request volume.

Attached are the raw p99 traces and error snippets (p99_logs.txt). This is impacting our checkout flow and causing user-visible timeouts. Our SLA margin is at risk and the CS queue is filling.

We need an immediate remediation path: rollback to previous profile or an emergency model fallback. Please advise fastest path and let us know if you need additional logs. If we can’t resolve quickly we will need credits and escalation to your execs.

—Sam
Sam Tan
Head of Platform Reliability, CadenzaAI

On Tue, Mar 28, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sam Tan <sam.tan@cadenza.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing a severe degradation ... since the new v4-compact quantization profile was rolled out

Preliminary triage summary (10:30 UTC):
- We reproduced a p99 spike locally with a replay using the v4-compact profile.
- Root cause signal: kernel selection under v4-compact seems to pick an aggressive fused attention path that increases memory fragmentation for KV caches on long-context streams. That fragmentation causes intermittent decode stalls and backpressure to the request queue, leading to higher latency and transient 5xx errors when memory oversubscription occurs on the dedicated pool.
- The model weights themselves didn't show accuracy regressions in our unit evals; this is performance-regression specific to the q-profile/hardware interaction.

Attachments: profile_diff.json (diff of runtime kernel choices and mem maps).

Mitigation options (ordered by speed):
1) Immediate: Perform a canary rollback of the pool to v4-standard (previous profile) and route 20% of traffic back, observe 15 minute window. Expected p99 recovery to ~140ms based on staging canary.
2) If rollback is not acceptable: enforce a temporary request-size limit and increase per-worker memory headroom; this reduces throughput further and is not ideal.
3) Root fix: refine the q-profile heuristics in the runtime so the fused kernels are gated by observed context-length distribution — takes days.

Recommend: execute option (1) now, then monitor.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SWE, Runtime Optimizations — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, sam.tan@cadenza.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production alert — marked latency & errors after last-night rollout

Quick canary results: we applied a rollback to v4-standard on a staging replica and replayed a 1-hour production window. Results attached (canary_metrics.csv). Highlights:
- p99: 960ms (v4-compact) -> 150ms (v4-standard) in canary under identical load.
- Error spike disappeared in the canary run.
- Throughput returned to ~95% of baseline.

Rollback operational notes:
- We can perform the rollback for your dedicated pool in a rolling fashion (20% buckets) to minimize client disruption. Full rollback of all nodes estimated ~25 minutes.
- Risk: during rolling windows, some buckets may still see higher latency; recommend scheduling immediate rollback now and monitoring for 30 minutes post-complete.

I propose we execute an immediate rollback at the next minimal-traffic window (in 15 minutes) unless we receive a block. Approvals needed: customer go-ahead (Sam), commercial exec sign-off for credits if SLA breach becomes necessary (Vanessa/Ben).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
